## Why the best teams win

The model trained on 256 knockout team-seasons to predict how far a club advances, using only their group or league-phase statistics from 15 seasons covering 488 team-seasons. Its predictive power is evident in a mean within-season Spearman correlation of 0.46 between predicted and actual stages, with an AUC of 0.72 for reaching the final. The model's Brier score stands at 0.098, slightly better than the base-rate guess which scored 0.103, though this edge was not tested as significant. In terms of identifying finalists, 46.7% of actual finalists appeared in the model's top 4 predictions for their respective seasons.

Regarding what drives deep runs, style and results play distinct roles compared to pedigree. The "style" feature set yields a Spearman correlation of 0.41 and an AUC of 0.69, while "results" achieves a higher correlation of 0.3 with an AUC of 0.72. Pedigree alone performs the weakest with a Spearman of 0.28 and an AUC of 0.66. The most important stat for deep runs is Attacks per game (style), with an importance score of 0.25, followed by Goal difference per game (results) at 0.201. Both are marked as robust, meaning the logistic model agrees on their direction in at least 12 of 15 seasons. Other robust stats include Long passes (% of passes) at 0.137 and Passes per game at 0.128. Conversely, Shot conversion is associated with lower values helping (importance 0.086), as are Fouls committed per game and Distance covered per game, though the latter lacks a robustness label in the top six.

## Winners vs runners-up

When comparing winners against runners-up across all 15 finals, the analysis relies on group or league-phase stats rather than final match events. The data shows that while some trends exist, no difference between winners and runners-up reaches statistical significance under the Holm-adjusted p threshold of 0.05. For instance, Pre-season UEFA club coefficient was higher for the winner in 13 finals with a mean z-score difference of 0.57, yet the adjusted p-value is 0.111. Similarly, winners committed fewer fouls per game (lower helps) in 12 instances compared to runners-up, resulting in a mean difference of -1.13 and an adjusted p of 0.181.

Other stats show mixed results without significant separation. Winners attempted more Shots per game in 11 finals (mean z: 0.79, p: 0.292) and had higher Pass accuracy in 12 cases (p: 0.422). However, for Points per game and Goal difference per game, the winners were higher in only a slight majority or tied scenarios, yielding adjusted p-values of 1.0. The comparison also reveals that winners did not consistently have lower Opponent shots on target, nor did they cover less distance, with all such comparisons resulting in Holm-adjusted p-values of 1.0. This indicates that while certain stats like Attacks per game are associated with deep runs generally, the specific differences between a season's winner and runner-up based on pre-final statistics do not meet the criteria for statistical significance in this dataset.

Quote every number exactly as it appears in the facts, with the same rounding. Do not introduce players, managers, matches, events, analyses or numbers that are not in the facts. 'Better than this %' figures say how many teams the club beat on a stat, so higher is always better, including for stats marked '(lower is better)', where beating a team means having the lower value. Write them as 'better than X% of teams', never as 'top X%'. SHAP contributions are measured in knockout stages: a positive contribution means the stat pushed the model's expected stage up by that fraction of a round, a negative one pushed it down. A SHAP contribution is the model's view, not a measure of how good the team was at the stat: a team can rank high on a stat the model marked down, so never call a stat a strength or a weakness because of its SHAP sign. Everything here is a statistical association, not a cause: never say a stat or a team's profile drove, powered, propelled, carried, helped, hindered or prevented a result, and do not explain why a stat got its contribution. Write plain markdown without tables.

Write 350-450 words of markdown in total, two paragraphs of about 100 words under each of exactly these two headings, in this order:
## Why the best teams win
## Winners vs runners-up

Explain which stats are associated with deep knockout runs and whether pedigree, results or style matters most, using the feature-set comparison. Say how well the model does by comparing its Brier score with the base-rate Brier score and stating how often finalists were in its top 4; the model's edge over the base-rate guess was not tested, so do not call it significant or superior. 'Importance' is the average size of a stat's push on the expected stage, in either direction. The model learns from the knockout team-seasons, using each team's group/league-phase stats. Only call a stat 'robust' if its robustness label is robust. Winners vs runners-up compares those same group/league-phase stats, not what happened in the final. Never call a winners-vs-runners-up difference significant unless its Holm-adjusted p is below the significance threshold in the facts.
